caller.name: Karen Doyle
caller.persona: worried mother trying to stay level, voice cracking at the edges, over-explaining
caller.openingLine: Hi, um, I don't know if this is the right thing but my daughter hasn't come home from school and it's been four hours and her phone's going straight to voicemail and that's just not her, she always answers me.
dontKnowLines: I don't know. God, I should know that, shouldn't I.
I don't know, I've been ringing everyone.

incident.summaryTruth: Karen Doyle reports her daughter Libby Doyle, 14, has not returned from Boundstone College, {{town}}. Last seen leaving school at 3:15pm by a friend, four hours ago. Phone off or dead, going straight to voicemail. No argument at home. Libby is described as white, 5ft 3, shoulder-length dyed red hair, school uniform with a black puffer coat, black rucksack. No previous missing episodes. Best friend Amelia has not seen her since the school gate. Libby recently mentioned an older boy called Connor she met online, mother does not know his surname, this had caused mild concern. Caller is at home at {{address}}, {{town}} with her younger son.

facts.label: Missing person's name and age
facts.beat: Libby. Libby Doyle, she's fourteen. Fifteen in October.

facts.label: Last confirmed sighting
facts.beat: Her friend saw her walking out the school gates at quarter past three. Boundstone College. Nobody's seen her since, that's four hours.

facts.label: Description
facts.value: white, 5ft 3, dyed red hair, school uniform, black puffer coat, black rucksack
facts.beat: She's five foot three, slim, her hair's dyed red, shoulder length. School uniform, and a black puffer coat, black rucksack.

facts.label: Phone status
facts.beat: Straight to voicemail every time since about four. It's never off. Even when she's sulking she reads the messages.

facts.label: Concerning online contact
facts.value: older boy called Connor, met online
facts.beat: There's... she mentioned a boy called Connor a few weeks back. Older. She met him online, I never got a surname. I told her I didn't like it. You don't think...

facts.label: Previous episodes
facts.beat: Never. Not once. That's why I'm ringing you and not just waiting.

facts.label: Argument at home
facts.beat: No, nothing. This morning was completely normal, she had her toast, she was singing in the bathroom.

escalations.text: Member of public reports a girl matching the description sat alone at Worthing pier shelter, matching black puffer coat and red hair.
